prompt.context_jp: 派手な身なりの女性が営業所に飛び込んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___、屋代が行きつけにしているバー「ちちんぷいぷい」のママ、こころだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the narrator identifying who this new person is.

feedback.correct_en: The woman has already been introduced visually in the previous sentence; now the narrator identifies who she is. 彼女 is the known topic, so は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 彼女 as new information, but she was already in view — the news here is her identity (ママのこころ), not her existence.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女は社長の娘だった。
contrast_examples.en: She was (as it turns out) the president's daughter.
It's she who is the president's daughter. (identifying from a group)

prompt.context_jp: こころは屋代に泣きつく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「大変なの！ 私のお店___追い出されちゃうの！」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Kokoro bursting in with urgent new information about her shop?

feedback.correct_en: Kokoro is delivering urgent new information in a single breath. が marks 私のお店 as the newly presented subject of the crisis.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 私のお店 as an already-established topic she's commenting on — but this is the very first time she's mentioning it; it's news.

contrast_examples.en: As for the shop, it's doing fine. (topic comment)

prompt.context_jp: こころが朝お店で見たことを話している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今朝 お店を出たら 黒いスーツの お兄さん___立ってたの」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits introducing someone she suddenly noticed outside her bar?

feedback.correct_en: She's reporting a new, unexpected sight — 'there was a man standing there.' が marks this fresh, perceived subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the man was already a known topic she's commenting on, but he's a stranger she just encountered.

contrast_examples.en: There's a cat in the garden. (noticed)

contrast_examples.jp: その猫はうちの猫です。

prompt.context_jp: ビルの他のテナントがみんな出て行ったと知って。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「えっ じゃあ 今残ってるの “ちちんぷいぷい”___？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'only Chichinpuipui is the one left'?

feedback.correct_en: Yashiro is confirming an exhaustive identification: of all tenants, only Chichinpuipui remains. だけ captures 'only / nothing but'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a mere topic comment, and が alone would miss the 'only' nuance that drives the surprise.

contrast_examples.jp: 残ってるのは彼だけだ。
contrast_examples.en: The only one left is him.
He is the one still here.

prompt.context_jp: 移転を勧められたこころの反論。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「だって あそこ___ 私のふるさとだもん」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'as for that place, it's my hometown'?

feedback.correct_en: あそこ refers to the shop they've been discussing — it's the established topic. She's making a statement about it: 'that place is my home.' は fits the X=Y topic-comment pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like she's picking out that place among others as the hometown, but here she's simply characterizing the known location.

contrast_examples.jp: あそこは私のふるさとです。

contrast_examples.en: That's the one that's my hometown. (contrastive identification)

prompt.context_jp: こころに「昔の私みたい」と言われた三軒家。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あなたと私___違います！」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Machi drawing a sharp line between herself and Kokoro?

feedback.correct_en: Machi is contrastively asserting the pair 'you and I' as the topic of difference. は carries the contrastive emphasis against being lumped together.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly focus on 'who differs' as new information, missing the you-vs-me contrast Machi is making.

prompt.context_jp: 空き部屋だらけのビルの描写。
prompt.prompt_jp: 空き部屋ばかりになったビルの中で、この店___けがぽつんと灯りをともしている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'only this one shop (vs the rest)'?

feedback.correct_en: The contrast is 'all other rooms are empty, but THIS shop alone has its light on.' だけ captures the exclusivity against the empty building.
feedback.incorrect_en: Plain が or は miss the 'only / alone' nuance explicit in ぽつんと. The scene demands exclusivity.

contrast_examples.jp: この店だけが開いている。

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の決め台詞。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私に売れない家___ない」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Machi's signature line 'there is no house I can't sell'?

feedback.correct_en: In existence/non-existence statements with 'ない', は marks the topic ('as for houses I can't sell, there are none'). It also carries a contrastive flavor fitting her defiant tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 家がない would simply report an absence; the actual line stages 売れない家 as the topic to deny, which は does.

contrast_examples.jp: 私にできないことはない。

prompt.context_jp: 足立が庭野に深川営業所の同期から聞いた噂を伝える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「深川の営業所に 同期___いるんだけどさ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces 'a colleague of mine' as new information?

feedback.correct_en: Adachi is introducing a new referent ('a colleague') for the first time. Existence/presentational clauses with いる take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose 同期 as a known topic, but Niwano hasn't heard about this person yet.

contrast_examples.en: That friend is funny. (now a topic)

prompt.context_jp: 娘を気遣う母、望月葵の言葉。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今のお家___階段が多くて カンナが退院しても 暮らしにくいでしょ？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets up 'our current house' as the topic being commented on?

feedback.correct_en: Aoi is making a statement about their current home (the topic), with the subordinate clause subject 階段 marked by が. The X は… Y が多い pattern is textbook topic-plus-descriptor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 家が would make 'house' the exhaustive subject of 階段が多い, breaking the natural double-subject frame where the house is the overarching topic.

prompt.context_jp: 病室の張りつめた沈黙を破ったのは誰か。
prompt.prompt_jp: 先に口を開いたのは、カンナの方___った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle identifies Kanna as the one who spoke first?

feedback.correct_en: The cleft 'のは Xだった' identifies X exhaustively — Kanna was the one who spoke. The copula だ closes the identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: が doesn't fit here because the slot is after のは…, which already does the exhaustive-listing work; the predicate just needs だった.

contrast_examples.jp: 最初に話したのは彼だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who spoke first was him.
He was the one who spoke first.

prompt.context_jp: カンナが母の本心を疑って吐き捨てる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ママ___私をダシにして パパから お金を搾り取ろうとしてるんだ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'as for Mom, she's using me…'?

feedback.correct_en: Kanna is making an accusation about her mother — a known topic — explaining what she thinks Mom is up to. は frames Mom as the topic with a long comment following.
feedback.incorrect_en: ママが would present Mom as newly identified subject (as if answering 'who is doing this?'), but Kanna is already talking about her.

contrast_examples.en: It's Mom who is dancing. / Mom is dancing (just noticed).

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家がカンナに母の秘密を明かす。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「毎夜 毎夜 お母様___踊っておられます」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Machi's revelation about Kanna's mother?

feedback.correct_en: お母様 is the known person on screen and the topic of Machi's narrative. は fits a measured, explanatory revelation about an established referent.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like a sudden reporting of 'who's dancing' — but Kanna already sees that it is her mother; what's new is the ongoing truth being told.

contrast_examples.jp: 母は毎晩働いています。
contrast_examples.en: Mom works every night. (telling about her)

prompt.context_jp: 屋代がこころに提案している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「そのお金___ どこか別の場所に 移転することを考えてみたら？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'with that money' as the means?

feedback.correct_en: で marks the means or instrument: using that money (compensation) to relocate.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination/time, and を would mark a direct object — neither fits 'by means of the money.'

contrast_examples.en: Buy a house with that money.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が室田に指示する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「5分後 応接ブース___ お茶」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the destination for bringing tea?

feedback.correct_en: に marks the destination (goal) toward which tea is to be delivered.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an action, not a goal of movement; を can't mark a destination here.

prompt.context_jp: 望月葵が三軒家に頼む。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「病院___お越しいただければ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the hospital as the place to come to?

feedback.correct_en: お越しいただく means 'come,' and に marks the destination/goal of coming.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the venue of an activity, not the goal of movement; を doesn't mark destinations for intransitive 来る.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が庭野に命じる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「この壁紙___剥がし 磨け」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'this wallpaper' as the direct object of 剥がす?

feedback.correct_en: 剥がす is transitive — 'to strip something off.' The thing being stripped (壁紙) takes を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it the subject of an intransitive, and に would make it a target/goal — neither fits a transitive command.

prompt.context_jp: 黒いスーツの男がこころに言った言葉。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「6ヶ月以内に ___ って 通達しましたけど」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb best fits 'you must vacate the premises'?

feedback.correct_en: 立ち退く is the legal/real-estate term for vacating premises under eviction. It matches the context of a land shark serving an eviction notice.
feedback.incorrect_en: 引っ越す is a neutral 'move house,' lacking the forced-eviction nuance. 出発する means 'depart' (for a trip).

contrast_examples.jp: 立ち退きを命じられる。

prompt.context_jp: こころの話を聞いた屋代の見立て。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「それ ___ っぽいな」
prompt.prompt_en: What term fits Yashiro's suspicion that this is a shady land-grab?

feedback.correct_en: 地上げ refers to buying up land (often by pressuring holdouts) to redevelop. The pattern of tenants vanishing one by one is a classic sign.
feedback.incorrect_en: 値上げ is 'price increase,' and 引っ越し is a neutral 'moving house' — neither captures the coercive land-grab scheme.

contrast_examples.jp: 家賃の値上げを通告された。
contrast_examples.en: I was notified of a rent increase.

prompt.context_jp: 屋代の助言。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「相当な金額の ___ が もらえることになるはず」
prompt.prompt_en: What's the term for the compensation paid to a tenant forced to vacate?

feedback.correct_en: 立ち退き料 is the compensation paid when a tenant is required to vacate. It's the specific real-estate term fitting the eviction context.
feedback.incorrect_en: 敷金 is a security deposit at move-in; 手数料 is a service/handling fee. Neither matches 'eviction compensation.'

prompt.context_jp: 一棟売却を宣言した屋代に布施が言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「しかし それはそれは なかなか ___ だよね」
prompt.prompt_en: What set phrase means 'an extremely difficult task'?

feedback.correct_en: 至難の業 means 'an extremely difficult feat.' Fuse is impressed-but-worried that selling a whole building is nearly impossible.
feedback.incorrect_en: 朝飯前 means 'a piece of cake' — opposite meaning. 一石二鳥 means 'two birds with one stone.'

prompt.context_jp: 足立が庭野をけしかける。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「目黒営業所を 5ヶ月で ___ ⇒ ウチの営業所に来たんだから」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'rebuilt/turned around' a struggling office?

feedback.correct_en: 立て直す means to turn around / restructure a struggling organization. It's the standard business idiom here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 片付ける is 'tidy up / finish off.' 建て直す (same pronunciation) specifically means 'rebuild a physical structure,' not reorganize a business.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家がカンナに厳しく言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「それを言い訳にするのは カンナ様が ___ からです」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'because you are running away from reality'?

feedback.correct_en: 逃げる in a metaphorical sense means 'to run away from / avoid confronting' something. Machi accuses Kanna of avoiding re-challenge.
feedback.incorrect_en: 休む (resting) and 怒る (being angry) don't match the accusation that she's dodging a dream she could still pursue.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が葵の心境を説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「踊らなければ 葵様は 自分が ___ なってしまうんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase expresses 'she won't be herself anymore'?

feedback.correct_en: The pattern X でなくなる = 'cease to be X'. 自分でなくなる = 'lose one's self.' This matches Kokoro's earlier 'アイデンティティーが崩壊' theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: でないに and じゃないで are ungrammatical in this frame — the connective form before なる must be でなく.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は昔の彼でなくなった。
contrast_examples.en: He is no longer the person he used to be.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が白洲に投げつけた言葉。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「自分の ___ で立つことは 不可能です」
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the idiom 'stand on your own feet'?

feedback.correct_en: 自分の足で立つ = 'to stand on one's own feet,' meaning to be independent. It's the standard idiom Machi uses to call Mika incapable of independence.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手 and 頭 don't form this idiom. 自分の手で means 'with one's own hands,' and 自分の頭で考える is 'think for oneself.'

contrast_examples.en: Stand on one's own two feet.

prompt.context_jp: 白洲が「売れそうです」と報告したときの三軒家の返し方。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural as Machi's cold, no-nonsense reply?

choices.text: 売れそうだということは まだ売れていないということです。
売れそうなことは まだ売れないことです。
売れそうなのは まだ売れていないんです。

feedback.correct_en: The X ということは Y ということです frame restates X as Y with cutting logic — perfect for Machi's blunt style. The original line uses exactly this parallelism.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 売れない (won't sell), changing the meaning. C's structure is broken — のは/んです don't balance into a clean restatement.

contrast_examples.jp: できそうだということは、できていないということだ。
contrast_examples.en: 'Looking likely to be done' means 'not yet done.'

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が応接ブースで客に名乗る場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which self-introduction sounds most natural for a real-estate agent greeting a client?

choices.text: 望月様、テーコー不動産の三軒家でございます。
望月さん、テーコー不動産の三軒家です。
望月様、テーコー不動産の三軒家だ。

feedback.correct_en: でございます + 様 is the standard business-polite register when greeting a client at an office. Machi uses this with customers despite her blunt personality.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is polite but too casual for a first client meeting; C's だ is plain form, inappropriate for a client greeting.

contrast_examples.jp: ABC商事の佐藤でございます。

prompt.context_jp: 足立が男らしい告白の例を芝居がかって演じる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as Adachi's theatrical, blunt-masculine 'stay with me'?

choices.text: そばに いてください

feedback.correct_en: いろよ is the rough masculine imperative of いる plus よ — exactly the drama-cliché 'stay by me' Adachi is parodying.
feedback.incorrect_en: いてください is politely requesting, killing the macho vibe. いなさい is a parent-to-child command, wrong register for a love line.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家がカンナにタブレットを差し出す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural coming from Machi (polite but firm) to Kanna?

choices.text: ご覧いただきたいものがあります。
見てもらいたいものがあるよ。
見せたいものがあるんだ。

feedback.correct_en: ご覧いただく is the honorific of 見てもらう. Machi consistently uses honorific keigo even with a hostile teenage client; this matches her exact line in the chapter.
feedback.incorrect_en: B and C are casual forms — Machi never shifts out of polite forms with 'お客様.' The honorific is what signals her professional distance.

contrast_examples.jp: こちらをご覧ください。
contrast_examples.en: Please take a look at this. (honorific)

prompt.context_jp: 珍しく強引な決断をしてきた屋代への部下の皮肉。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'that's unusual for you'?

choices.text: 課長にしては珍しく、強引に決めてきましたね。
課長なのに珍しく、強引に決めてきましたね。
課長によって珍しく、強引に決めてきましたね。

feedback.correct_en: X にしては Y = 'given that it's X, Y is unexpected.' It's the standard frame for 'unusual for someone of X's type.'
feedback.incorrect_en: のに implies contradictory concession ('despite being manager'), which is odd here. によって means 'depending on' and doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供にしてはしっかりしている。
子供なのにしっかりしている。
contrast_examples.en: Even though he's a kid, he's mature.
